en: The Jātaka: The Sixth Book of Birth Stories,
Chapter on the Son Kharaputta.
5. The Mayhaka Bird Jātaka:
“There was a bird named Mayhaka, who roamed through mountain clefts and valleys;”
Having climbed a ripe *pippali* tree, he cries out, "It is mine! It is mine!
While he is thus lamenting,
The flocks of birds gathered together;
having eaten the long pepper, they departed,
while that bird merely lamented.
In the same way, someone here may have accumulated much wealth,
yet neither for themselves nor for their kinsmen,
He practices according to his resolve.
He does not [cling to] clothing, food, garlands, or ointments.
He experiences something for himself alone and does not provide for his kinsmen;
while he is thus lamenting, [the time passes].
For one who guards things thinking "this is mine,
this is mine," kings, or thieves,
or even unpleasant heirs [will take them].
They depart taking the wealth,
while that man merely laments; the wise person,
having attained riches, [remains steadfast].
And he supports his kinsmen;
by that he attains fame and,
after passing away, rejoices in heaven.
The Mahākajaṭā Jātaka, the fifth.
